cases.architecture: Express 5 REST service with Drizzle ORM over Postgres (node-postgres pool), session identity resolved by middleware from the signed fw_session cookie.
cases.why: req.query.lane and req.query.sort are pasted into a sql.raw statement, so a lane term such as RO' OR 1=1 -- or an arbitrary ORDER BY expression is executed as SQL text against rate_cards for every logged in desk user.

cases.architecture: Express 5 REST service with Drizzle ORM over Postgres (node-postgres pool), session identity resolved by middleware from the signed fw_session cookie.
cases.why: Same hand written statement and the same dynamic ORDER BY, but the lane term is bound as a parameter inside a sql template (with its ILIKE metacharacters escaped) and the sort column can only be one of the three keys in SORT_COLUMNS, so no request text reaches the SQL string.

cases.architecture: Express 5 REST service with Drizzle ORM over Postgres (node-postgres pool), session identity resolved by middleware from the signed fw_session cookie.
cases.why: The detail handler filters on eq(consignments.reference, ...) alone; session.forwarderId is read but never enters the predicate, so any authenticated desk user can read another branch's consignment together with its carrier rates and customs document list.

cases.architecture: Express 5 REST service with Drizzle ORM over Postgres (node-postgres pool), session identity resolved by middleware from the signed fw_session cookie.
cases.why: findOwnConsignment resolves the reference with and(eq(reference), eq(forwarderId, session.forwarderId)) before any event is read and answers 404 for a foreign reference, so the events query only ever receives an id from the caller's own branch.

cases.architecture: Express 5 REST service with Drizzle ORM over Postgres (node-postgres pool), session identity resolved by middleware from the signed fw_session cookie.
cases.why: req.params.fileName reaches path.join(CUSTOMS_ROOT, consignment.customsFolder, ...) behind nothing but an extension test, so ../../<other-forwarder>/CNS-2026-000001/declaration.pdf leaves the consignment folder and the stream serves another branch's customs paperwork.

cases.architecture: Express 5 REST service with Drizzle ORM over Postgres (node-postgres pool), session identity resolved by middleware from the signed fw_session cookie.
cases.why: The requested name is reduced with path.basename and matched against a strict capture-name pattern, and the resolved path must start with PROOF_ROOT + path.sep before the stream is opened; the folder comes from a row already scoped to the caller's forwarder.

cases.architecture: Express 5 REST service with Drizzle ORM over Postgres (node-postgres pool), session identity resolved by middleware from the signed fw_session cookie.
cases.why: HMAC verification only runs inside if (signature && secret), so a callback with no x-carrier-signature header - or one naming a carrier that has no configured secret - skips verification and still inserts tracking events and updates consignments.status for any reference.

cases.architecture: Express 5 REST service with Drizzle ORM over Postgres (node-postgres pool), session identity resolved by middleware from the signed fw_session cookie.
cases.why: A missing secret, signature or timestamp is a 401 before the body is even parsed, the timestamp must fall inside a five minute window, and the HMAC over timestamp.body is compared with crypto.timingSafeEqual after a length check, so no unsigned callback reaches the tracking insert or the status update.

cases.architecture: Express 5 REST service with Drizzle ORM over Postgres (node-postgres pool), session identity resolved by middleware from the signed fw_session cookie.
cases.why: req.body is spread straight into .set(), so beyond pickup time and service level a caller can write status, agreedRateCents, approvedBy and consignmentId - self-confirming a booking, rewriting the agreed rate, or re-pointing the booking at another branch's consignment.

cases.architecture: Express 5 REST service with Drizzle ORM over Postgres (node-postgres pool), session identity resolved by middleware from the signed fw_session cookie.
cases.why: The patch is parsed by a .strict() zod schema holding only the three editable fields and the update names those columns explicitly, so status and approvedBy can only be moved by the separate decision endpoint behind requireRole('admin').

cases.architecture: Express 5 REST service with Drizzle ORM over Postgres (node-postgres pool), session identity resolved by middleware from the signed fw_session cookie.
cases.why: When the signed cookie is absent the middleware base64url-decodes the plain fw_partner cookie from req.cookies and takes partnerId, carrierCode, forwarderId and scopes from it, so any client that sets that cookie itself chooses which carrier and which forwarder it acts as.

cases.architecture: Express 5 REST service with Drizzle ORM over Postgres (node-postgres pool), session identity resolved by middleware from the signed fw_session cookie.
cases.why: Identity is taken only from req.signedCookies.fw_session - the typeof token !== 'string' check rejects the false that cookie-parser stores for a bad signature - and the token is re-resolved against a non-expired, non-revoked session joined to a live user, so the forwarder id is server derived and req.cookies is never consulted.
